subject: Cross-border data guardrails & handover for private deployment
messages:
From: Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@globex-retail.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: rc.security@globex-retail.com, infra@tokyo-retail.jp
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Redwood private deploy — data locality & DR questions

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we move toward scoping the private deployment for Globex Retail (EU + APAC), our legal and security teams flagged a few non-standard asks that we need clarified before we sign the SOW:

1) Active-data residency: We need assurance that PII originating from EU tenants never leaves EU-hosted compute or encrypted storage at rest — including backups and KV caches.
2) Cross-region failover: For APAC, we want a warm-standby model that avoids replicating EU PII into APAC unless explicitly authorized.
3) Network peering constraints: Our Tokyo infra team requires explicit CIDR-level peering rules (no implicit routes) and a list of endpoints for your control plane calls.
4) Audit evidence: SOC2 & architecture evidence showing the network diagram, peering rules, and backup retention for both regions.

I've attached the internal security checklist (we'll send a formal questionnaire after this note). Can you confirm whether Redwood supports keeping KV caches region-scoped, and if you can provide a failover handover runbook for our ops team?

Appreciate a short summary and proposed next steps by end of day Wed (07 Apr).

Best,
Emma
Emma Lopez
Head of Cloud Operations, Globex Retail
Attachment: globex_security_checklist_v1.pdf
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
To: Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@globex-retail.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 13:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Redwood private deploy — data locality & DR questions

Emma — thanks for the clear summary. High level answers up front, then a proposed plan:

- KV cache locality: Yes — Redwood supports per-tenant KV cache pinning to a region and will not replicate that cache to other regions unless configured. We use encrypted, local ephemeral disk for KV plus periodic encrypted snapshots; snapshots for EU-tenants can be configured to remain within EU storage buckets.
- Warm-standby approach: We can implement warm-standby for APAC that maintains model weights and metadata in a separate APAC pool but keeps customer data (PII indexes, session logs) isolated until an approved failover event.
- Peering & endpoints: We'll provide a CIDR-level peering proposal and a list of control plane endpoints (region-scoped) for your network team.
- Audit artifacts: We can produce the architecture diagram, peering rules, and a short evidence pack for SOC2 review.

Proposed next steps (timeline):
1) Today — Redwood to share initial network diagram + residency matrix (attached).
2) Tue (06 Apr) — Karthik to run a short live session with Globex infra to confirm CIDRs and route tables.
3) Wed (07 Apr) — Provide a draft failover handover runbook and peering rules; Globex security provides areas that need redlines.
4) Thu (08 Apr) — Lock SOW language for residency and DR clauses; deliverables listed.

I'm looping in Karthik (networking lead), Marcus (private deploy PM), and Soojin (compliance) to move each item. If Globex prefers, we can template the canary/failover RACI in the runbook.

Attachments: network_diagram_v2.png, residency_matrix_q1_2027.csv

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@globex-retail.com>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 02:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Redwood private deploy — data locality & DR questions

Hi Emma / team,

Quick note from networking: attached is a draft peering rules file (peering_rules_draft.txt) that enumerates required CIDR ranges, allowed ports, and mandatory egress/ingress filters. A few implementation notes:

- We will publish region-scoped control-plane IP ranges and FQDNs; control-plane calls will be TLS+mTLS (customer can require mTLS).
- For KV caches we propose using a per-tenant VPC endpoint and a network ACL that only allows the regional serving pool to attach to that endpoint. That prevents accidental cross-region attach.
- Backups: snapshots will be stored in region-specific object storage; cross-region copy requires signed authorization from a Globex owner.

Requested from Globex: the exact Tokyo CIDR block to include in the peering file and whether central NAT is used for outbound control-plane calls.

I'll be available for the Tue session at 09:00 JST / 00:00 UTC — but can shift earlier if needed.

Regards,
Karthik
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: peering_rules_draft.txt
From: Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@globex-retail.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: rc.security@globex-retail.com, infra@tokyo-retail.jp, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 16:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Redwood private deploy — data locality & DR questions

Thanks all — that helps a lot. Short replies and items we can action: 

- Tokyo CIDR: infra@tokyo-retail.jp will provide the /20 tomorrow morning JST.
- mTLS: Security requests mTLS on control-plane endpoints; we'll add that to the questionnaire.
- Failover runbook: Please include an explicit checklist that our on-call runs when executing a cross-border failover (including who signs the authorization, how to scrub PII indices, expected RTO/RPO for EU vs APAC).
- Evidence pack: send the SOC2-relevant artifacts to rc.security@globex-retail.com (we'll track in the ticket).

We can confirm SOW language once we have the runbook and the peering file locked. Appreciate the quick turnaround — scheduling the Tuesday sync for 09:00 JST.

Emma
--
Emma Lopez
Head of Cloud Operations, Globex Retail
Attachment: globex_notes_from_meeting.txt
